title: Fixed Prepositions: Verb, Adjective & Noun Combinations
subtitle: Complete Reference Guide to Collocations, Semantic Contrasts, Direct-Object Verbs, and Administrative Legal Patterns
overview: English grammar mein sabhi prepositions spatio-temporal logic par nahi chalte. Bahut se words kisi specific preposition ke sath ek natural grammatical unit (Collocation) banate hain jise hum Fixed Prepositions kehte hain. Rajasthan High Court System Assistant examination mein Verb + Preposition, Adjective + Preposition, Noun + Preposition combinations, confusing pairs (jaise agree with vs agree to, result in vs result from), direct-object verbs (jahan preposition omit hota hai), preposition ke baad gerund (-ing) forms, aur administrative/legal collocations par frequently questions puche jaate hain. Is comprehensive guide mein sabhi core combinations aur unke structural mechanics ko simple Roman Hinglish mein master karein.

sections.title: Foundation: Understanding Fixed Preposition Combinations
sections.summary: Fixed Prepositions kya hote hain, collocations ka logic, semantic shifts, aur complete phrase learning strategy.
sections.content:
English language mein har preposition ko sirf 'in = mein' ya 'on = par' ke literal translation se decide nahi kiya ja sakta. Bahut saare Verbs, Adjectives, aur Nouns aise hote hain jo kisi ek specific preposition ke sath pair hokar ek idiomatic ya established syntactic unit banate hain. Inhe Fixed Prepositions ya Prepositional Collocations kaha jata hai.

1. Teen Core Combinations:
- Verb + Preposition: 'He relies ON his assistant.' / 'She apologized FOR the delay.'
- Adjective + Preposition: 'She is aware OF the consequences.' / 'He is eligible FOR promotion.'
- Noun + Preposition: 'What is the reason FOR the delay?' / 'There is no solution TO this problem.'

2. Semantic Shifts (Preposition Badalna = Meaning Badalna):
Aksar ek hi root word ke sath preposition badal jane se sentence ka meaning completely transform ho jata hai:
- 'Agree with a person' (Kisi vyakti ki baat ya vichar se sahmat hona: 'I agree with you.')
- 'Agree to a proposal' (Kisi plan ya terms ko formal consent dena: 'The registry agreed to the proposal.')
- 'Apply for a post' (Kisi vacancy ya position ke liye application dena: 'applied for the clerk post')
- 'Apply to an authority' (Kisi official body ya institution ko submit karna: 'applied to the High Court')
- 'Good at' (Kisi skill ya subject mein nipun hona: 'good at drafting')
- 'Good for' (Health ya benefit ke liye upyogi hona: 'Exercise is good for health')

3. Established Patterns vs Absolute Universal Laws:
Fixed prepositions ko rigid mathematical formulas ke roop mein nahi, balki English usage ke standard patterns ke roop mein samajhna chahiye. English mein variations aur evolving usages bhi hote hain (jaise 'different from' standard British hai, jabki 'different to' British informal mein aur 'different than' American English mein chalta hai; lekin Rajasthan exams mein 'different from' ko gold standard maana jata hai). Isliye exam perspective se established standard collocations ko priority di jaati hai.

4. Phrase Learning Strategy vs Isolated Memorization:
Isolated words yaad karne ke bajaye hamesha poori 3-word phrase yaad karni chahiye:
- Ratne ka galat tarika: 'depend = on', 'accuse = of', 'eligible = for'.
- Sahi contextual tarika: 'depend ON someone's advice', 'accuse someone OF theft', 'eligible FOR the examination'. Isse exam mein blank dekhte hi natural intuition trigger hoti hai.

categories.detail: Dekhein ki preposition ke baad aane wala word kya hai: Person hai (with/to), Thing/Topic hai (about/for), ya Action/Gerund hai (-ing).

sections.title: Verb + Preposition Combinations: High-Frequency Patterns
sections.summary: Examinations mein frequently aane wale Verb + Preposition collocations aur unke precise contextual meanings.
sections.content:
Rajasthan High Court aur doosre competitive exams mein verbs ke sath specific prepositions ke questions constant feature hote hain. Yahan high-yield verb combinations unke context aur sentence examples ke sath diye gaye hain:

1. Combinations with 'ON':
- depend on: Kisi vyakti ya condition par aashrit hona ('You can depend on his legal advice.')
- rely on: Bharosa ya vishwas karna ('The bench relies on authenticated forensic evidence.')
- insist on: Kisi baat par aadhikarik zidd ya zor dena ('The defense counsel insisted on filing a rejoinder.')
- congratulate someone on: Kisi uplabdhi par badhai dena ('We congratulated him on his appointment as magistrate.') [Note: NOT *congratulated for!]

2. Combinations with 'OF':
- approve of: Kisi baat ya aacharan ko anumodan ya sahmat dena ('The registrar did not approve of his misconduct.')
- accuse someone of: Kisi par apradh ya dosh lagana ('The police accused him of fabricating evidence.') [Note: NOT *accused for!]
- consist of: Kisi chiz se milkar banna / samahit hona ('The High Court bench consists of two learned judges.')
- despair of: Kisi chiz ki aasha chhod dena ('Never despair of achieving justice.')

3. Combinations with 'FOR':
- blame someone for: Kisi galti ke liye doshi thehrana ('Do not blame the assistant for the technical glitch.')
- apply for: Kisi post, scheme, ya leave ke liye aavedan karna ('He applied for the post of System Assistant.')
- apologize for: Kisi galti ya aacharan ke liye kshama maangna ('He apologized for the inadvertent delay.')
- search for / look for: Kisi khoi hui ya nayi chiz ko talashna ('The clerk is searching for the misplaced case file.')

4. Combinations with 'WITH':
- comply with: Rules, orders, ya guidelines ka palan karna ('All judicial officers must comply with the High Court circular.')
- deal with: Kisi mamle, subject ya person ko handle karna ('The Special Bench will deal with constitutional petitions.')
- cope with: Mushkil situation ko manage karna ('The staff struggled to cope with the sudden surge in filings.') [Note: Strictly 'cope with', NEVER *cope up with!]
- collide with: Kisi dusri chiz se takrana ('The vehicle collided with a stationary truck.')

5. Combinations with 'TO':
- refer to: Kisi document, rule, ya vyakti ka hawala dena ('The advocate referred to a landmark Supreme Court judgment.')
- belong to: Kisi ka swami ya hissa hona ('This judicial chamber belongs to the Chief Justice.')
- apply to: Kisi authority ko request bhejna ('The petitioner applied to the District Magistrate.')
- object to: Kisi baat ya proposal par aapti jatana ('The public prosecutor objected to the grant of bail.')
- prefer X to Y: Ek chiz ko dusri chiz se zyada pasand karna ('He prefers mediation to prolonged litigation.') [Note: NEVER *prefer than!]

6. Combinations with 'FROM':
- suffer from: Kisi bimari ya peeda se grasit hona ('The witness was suffering from acute illness.')
- recover from: Bimari ya shock se theek hona ('He has fully recovered from the injury.')
- prevent someone from: Kisi ko kuch karne se rokna ('The police prevented the crowd from entering the premises.')
- prohibit / abstain / refrain from: Door rehna ya bachna ('Judges must refrain from expressing personal opinions outside court.')

7. Combinations with 'IN':
- believe in: Ishwar, siddhant, ya kisi ke samarthya par vishwas rakhna ('We firmly believe in the rule of law.')
- confide in: Kisi par vishwas karke apna secret batana ('She confided in her senior colleague regarding the issue.')
- succeed in: Kisi prayas mein safal hona ('The police succeeded in tracing the missing files.')

8. Causal Pairs with 'RESULT':
- result in: Ka parinaam hona / lead to (Outcome): 'Careless typing resulted in a serious judicial error.'
- result from: Ki wajah se paida hona / arise from (Cause): 'The serious judicial error resulted from careless typing.'
Notice how reversing the subject and object reverses the preposition choice!

dimensions.name: Prepositional Verb Syntactic Formats
dimensions.description: Verb ke baad object aur preposition ki positioning ke structural formulas.

categories.name: Verb + Preposition + Object
categories.detail: Direct combination jahan verb ke turant baad preposition aata hai: rely on (someone), comply with (rules), belong to (society), consist of (members).

categories.name: Verb + Person + Preposition + Thing
categories.detail: Split combination jahan pehle person object aata hai phir preposition: accuse [someone] OF [theft], blame [someone] FOR [delay], prevent [someone] FROM [leaving].

categories.name: Two-Term Contrast: Prefer X TO Y
categories.detail: Do entities ke comparison mein preposition 'TO' lagta hai: prefer drafting to arguing, prefer tea to coffee. Examiner yahan 'than' lagakar trap karta hai.

dimensions.name: High-Yield Exam Collocation Traps
dimensions.description: Aam taur par boli jane wali galtiyan jo exams mein negative marks dilati hain.

categories.name: Congratulate ON (Not For)
categories.detail: Hindi mein 'safalta ke liye badhai' bolte hain, lekin English mein strictly 'congratulate someone ON success' hota hai.

categories.name: Cope WITH (Never Cope Up With)
categories.detail: Indian English mein 'cope up with' bolna common slang hai, par standard English aur exams mein 'cope with' strictly valid hai ('cope up' fatal error hai).

categories.name: Consist OF (Not Comprise OF)
categories.detail: 'Consist' hamesha 'of' leta hai ('consists of three parts'). Lekin 'comprise' direct object leta hai ('comprises three parts', NO 'of'!).

sections.formulaNote: REVERSAL VECTOR: 'A resulted IN B' (A caused B). 'B resulted FROM A' (B was caused by A). Always check whether the subject is the cause or the outcome.

sections.title: Adjective + Preposition Combinations: Evaluative, Mental & Relational States
sections.summary: Adjectives ke sath aane wale high-yield fixed prepositions, ability markers, aur Latin comparatives.
sections.content:
Adjectives kisi person ya situation ki quality, mental state, emotional response ya capacity ko express karte hain. Jab unke target ya scope ko sentence mein specify karna ho, toh specific prepositions lagte hain:

1. Mental State & Awareness:
- aware of: Parichit ya sajag hona ('The magistrate was fully aware of the legal precedents.')
- conscious of: Apne aacharan ya vatavaran ke prati chetan hona ('He was conscious of his administrative responsibility.')
- ignorant of: Anjan hona ('Ignorance of the law is no excuse.')
- afraid of: Kisi chiz ya vyakti se dar lagna ('The witness was afraid of testifying openly.')
- capable of: Kisi kaam ko karne ki kshamata rakhna ('She is capable of handling complex network administration.')
- devoid of: Se poori tarah vanchit ya khali hona ('The petition is completely devoid of merits.')

2. Ability & Performance: 'Good at' vs 'Good for':
- good at / bad at: Kisi subject, skill, sports, ya activity mein nipun ya kamzor hona ('He is exceptionally good at English grammar.' / 'She is bad at mathematics.')
- good for: Swasthya, labh, ya kisi uddeshya ke liye upyogi hona ('Fresh air is good for your health.' / 'This judicial order is good for five years.')
- quick at: Tez hona ('She is quick at calculating figures.')
- adept in / skilled in: Kisi art ya craft mein nipun hona ('He is skilled in computer forensics.')

3. Emotional Response & Relations:
- satisfied with / pleased with: Kisi ke kaam ya result se santusht hona ('The Bench was satisfied with the report.')
- angry with a person: Kisi vyakti par gussa hona ('The judge was angry with the defense lawyer.')
- angry at / about a situation: Kisi baat, aacharan ya ghatna par gussa hona ('The public was angry at the administrative delay.')
- concerned about: Kisi issue ya health ke baare mein chintit hona ('Citizens are concerned about data privacy.')
- concerned with: Kisi mudde se sambandhit hona ('This writ is concerned with fundamental rights.')

4. Eligibility & Liability:
- eligible for: Kisi post, exam, ya scheme ke liye patra hona ('Candidates with MCA are eligible for the System Assistant post.')
- liable for: Kisi fine, damage ya obligation ke liye kanoonan zimmedar hona ('The contractor is liable for damages.')
- liable to: Kisi bimari, dhand ya risk ki sambhavna hona ('Violators are liable to imprisonment up to two years.')
- responsible for: Kisi kaam, kriya ya result ke liye utardayi hona ('The registrar is responsible for scheduling hearings.')

5. Habitual & Tendency States:
- accustomed to: Aadi ya abhyast hona ('He is accustomed to working late hours in the registry.') [Note: Followed by Gerund -ing!]
- prone to: Kisi galti, bimari ya khatre ki aashanka hona ('This old IT server is prone to frequent crashes.')
- addicted to: Kisi buri aadat ka shikar hona ('He was addicted to gambling.')

6. Similarity & Difference:
- similar to: Ke jaisa ya saman hona ('His legal argument was remarkably similar to the earlier case.')
- different from: Se alag hona ('Indian constitutional law is different from the British convention.') [Standard exam choice: 'different from'.]
- consistent with: Ke anukool ya anuroop hona ('His statement is fully consistent with the forensic records.')

7. Latin Comparatives (Senior, Junior, Superior, Inferior, Prior, Anterior, Posterior):
Latin adjectives jinke end mein '-or' aata hai, wo comparison mein kabhi bhi 'THAN' nahi lete. Inke sath strictly preposition 'TO' lagta hai:
- senior to: 'He is three years senior to me in judicial service.' [NOT: *senior than me!]
- junior to: 'She is junior to all the officers in the department.'
- superior to: 'This network configuration is superior to the older setup.'
- inferior to: 'Substandard equipment is inferior to our required specifications.'
- prior to: 'Prior to the filing of the chargesheet, an investigation was conducted.'

sections.title: Noun + Preposition Combinations: Structural Connectors
sections.summary: Nouns ke sath aane wale fixed prepositions, cause vs reason, solution, access, aur demand patterns.
sections.content:
Sentences mein jab Nouns complex ideas, relationships, causes, ya solutions ko express karte hain, toh wo specific prepositions ke sath judte hain:

1. Reason vs Cause:
- reason for: Kisi action, event ya decision ke peeche ka justification ya explanation ('What is your reason for seeking an adjournment?') [Verb: reason with a person]
- cause of: Kisi incident, tragedy ya bimari ka direct physical origin ya source ('The investigation revealed the cause of the fire.')

2. Solutions, Keys & Access (Preposition 'TO'):
- solution to: Kisi samasya ya sawal ka hal ('We need an urgent solution to the case backlog.') [NOT: *solution of!]
- key to: Safalta ya kisi rahasya ki chabi ('Hard work is the key to passing the High Court exam.') [NOT: *key of!]
- access to: Kisi jagah, data ya suvidha tak pahunch ('Only authorized system assistants have access to the central server.')
- invitation to: Kisi event ka nimantran ('an invitation to the judicial seminar')
- damage to: Kisi property ya vyakti ko nuksan ('The flood caused extensive damage to the court archives.')
- reply / response to: Kisi letter ya notice ka jawab ('In reply to your query, we confirm the date.')
- exception to: Kisi general niyam ka apvad ('There is an exception to every general rule.')

3. Demand, Need & Request (Preposition 'FOR'):
- demand for: Kisi chiz ki bazaar ya samaj mein maang ('There is a massive demand for cyber security experts.')
- need for: Kisi chiz ki aavashyakta ('There is an urgent need for judicial infrastructure reforms.')
- desire for: Kisi chiz ki ichha ('a strong desire for career growth')
- appetite for: Kisi chiz ki ruchi ya bhookh ('an appetite for legal research')
- pity for: Kisi ke prati daya ('have pity for the poor')

4. Influence, Effect & Impact (Preposition 'ON'):
- effect on: Kisi chiz ya vyakti par prabhav ('The new legal ruling had a decisive effect on pending appeals.') [Noun: effect ON; Verb: affect something (NO prep!)]
- influence on: Prabhav dalna ('His mentor had a profound influence on his legal career.')
- impact on: Asar ('The economic policy had a severe impact on small businesses.')

5. Quantitative Shifts (Preposition 'IN'):
- increase in: Sankhya ya matra mein badhotari ('There is a sharp increase in online litigation filings.')
- decrease in / decline in: Kami hona ('a notable decline in administrative complaints')
- rise in / fall in: Utar-chadhaw ('a sudden rise in IT hardware costs')

6. Relational & Associative Nouns:
- relationship with a person: Sambandh ('She maintains a cordial relationship with her colleagues.')
- relationship between two entities: Do chizon ka aapsi sambandh ('the relationship between speed and accuracy')
- interest in: Kisi subject ya activity mein ruchi ('He developed a keen interest in administrative law.')
- awareness of: Kisi mudde ki jankari ('raising public awareness of digital security')
- responsibility for: Kisi galti ya task ka zimma ('take responsibility for the network outage')

dimensions.name: Classic Noun Preposition Traps
dimensions.description: Aam taur par dekhi jane wali galtiyan jahan galat preposition lagaya jata hai.

categories.name: Solution TO (Not 'Of')
categories.detail: Hindi mein 'samasya KA hal' bolte hain, isliye log '*solution of the problem' likh dete hain. Standard English mein strictly 'solution TO' hota hai.

categories.name: Key TO (Not 'Of')
categories.detail: 'Key of success' common Indian error hai; standard English collocation strictly 'key TO success' hai.

categories.name: Effect ON vs Affect (No Prep)
categories.detail: Noun 'effect' preposition 'ON' leta hai ('effect on health'). Lekin Verb 'affect' direct transitive hota hai aur koi preposition nahi leta ('Smoking affects health', NOT *affects on health!).

sections.formulaNote: NOUN FORMULA: 'Solution TO', 'Key TO', 'Reason FOR', 'Cause OF', 'Increase IN', 'Effect ON'. Memorize: Problems take solutions TO; success takes keys TO.

sections.title: Confusing Preposition Pairs: Precision Discrimination
sections.summary: Similar expressions jo context ke hisaab se preposition badalte hain: Agree, Apply, Accuse/Blame, Result, Compare, Complain, Good, Angry.
sections.content:
Rajasthan High Court exams mein distractor options create karne ke liye examiners confusing preposition pairs ka use karte hain. Ye expressions superficial roop se similar lagte hain lekin unke peeche strict contextual distinction hoti hai:

1. Agree WITH vs Agree TO:
- Agree WITH + Person / Opinion: Jab aap kisi vyakti se ya uske personal vichar se sahmat hote hain ('I completely agree with the advocate on this point.')
- Agree TO + Proposal / Plan / Terms: Jab aap kisi formal prastav, agreement, ya sujhaye gaye schedule ko accept karte hain ('The High Court administration agreed to the union's proposal for revised timings.')
- Agree ON + Matter / Subject: Jab do ya zyada parties milkar kisi vishay par common decision leti hain ('Both parties finally agreed on the settlement amount.')

2. Apply TO vs Apply FOR:
- Apply FOR + Post / Job / Leave / Grant: Jiske liye aavedan kiya ja raha hai ('She applied for the post of System Assistant.')
- Apply TO + Person / Authority / Institution: Jisko ya jis authority ke samne aavedan submit kiya ja raha hai ('He applied to the Registrar General for casual leave.')
- Apply TO + Rule / Situation: Jab koi niyam kisi par lagu hota hai ('This service rule applies to all court employees.')

3. Accuse OF vs Blame FOR:
- Accuse + Person + OF + Crime / Fault: Apradh ya dosh ka arop lagana ('The police accused him OF fabricating official records.') [Never: *accused for!]
- Blame + Person + FOR + Mistake: Kisi ko galti ka zimmedar thehrana ('The supervisor blamed the technician FOR the server failure.')
- Blame + Mistake + ON + Person: Galti ko kisi par madhna ('He blamed the data loss ON the power outage.')

4. Result IN vs Result FROM:
- Result IN = Outcome / Consequence (Parinaam hona / Produce): 'Negligence in verification resulted IN wrongful appointments.'
- Result FROM = Origin / Source (Wajah se hona / Be caused by): 'The wrongful appointments resulted FROM negligence in verification.'

5. Compare WITH vs Compare TO:
- Compare WITH: Jab do similar entities ko examine karke unke beech ke similarities aur differences dono ko evaluate kiya jaye ('Compare the Indian Constitution with the American Constitution.')
- Compare TO: Jab kisi ek chiz ko kisi poori tarah alag chiz se metaphorical likeness (roopak) batane ke liye compare kiya jaye ('Shakespeare compared the world to a stage.')

6. Complain OF vs Complain ABOUT:
- Complain OF: Kisi physical pain, symptom, ya bimari ka jikr karna ('The prisoner complained of severe chest pain.')
- Complain ABOUT: Kisi inconvenience, vyakti, service, ya situation ki shikayat karna ('The staff complained about the faulty air-conditioning.')
- Complain TO: Jisko shikayat ki jaye ('They complained to the Registrar.')

7. Good AT vs Good FOR:
- Good AT: Kisi subject, art, ya competence mein nipun hona ('He is very good at English transcription.')
- Good FOR: Swasthya, fayda, ya validity ke liye upyogi hona ('Regular typing practice is good for speed.')

8. Angry WITH vs Angry AT / ABOUT:
- Angry WITH + Person: Kisi vyakti par naraz hona ('The Chief Justice was angry with the public prosecutor.')
- Angry AT / ABOUT + Thing / Behavior: Kisi baat, galti, ya vyavhar par naraz hona ('He was angry at the unreasonable delay.')

9. Prefer X TO Y (Never 'Than'):
- Standard Formula: Prefer + Noun/Gerund + TO + Noun/Gerund
- Correct: 'He prefers drafting to arguing in court.' / 'I prefer coffee to tea.'
- Incorrect: *He prefers drafting than arguing. / *I prefer coffee than tea.

10. Different FROM (Standard Preference):
- Standard English: 'My legal opinion is different from yours.'
- Avoid in formal exams: '*different than' (American informal) ya '*different to' (British informal). Exams mein strictly 'different from' ko select karein.

dimensions.name: High Court Examiner Favorites
dimensions.description: Rajasthan High Court tests mein recurring pair questions.

categories.name: Prefer ... TO ...
categories.detail: Comparative blank jahan 'than' sabse common distractor hota hai. Answer strictly 'TO' hoga.

categories.name: Agree TO the proposal
categories.detail: Sentence mein 'proposal' ya 'terms' dekhein toh jaldbazi mein 'with' na lagayein; answer 'TO' hoga.

categories.name: Accused OF (Not For)
categories.detail: 'He was accused of bribery' (never *accused for bribery). But 'punished for bribery'.

sections.formulaNote: PAIR CONCORD RULE: Agree WITH a person, but agree TO a proposal. Apply TO an authority, but apply FOR a post. Accused OF a crime, but blamed FOR a mistake.

sections.title: Direct-Object Verbs: When No Extra Preposition Is Needed
sections.summary: Transitive verbs jo standard English mein direct object leti hain aur unnecessary prepositions ko reject karti hain.
sections.content:
Competitive examinations mein Preposition section ka ek sabse bada hissa 'Error Spotting' aur 'Sentence Improvement' hota hai jahan examiner aise verbs ke sath extra preposition lagakar test karta hai jo standard English mein strictly ZERO PREPOSITION (Direct Object) leti hain.

1. The Transitive Direct-Object Principle:
Transitive verbs ka action seedhe unke direct object par pass over hota hai. Unke aur object ke beech kisi preposition ki zaroorat nahi hoti. Hindi ke bolchal ke translation se influence hokar candidates aksar galat prepositions insert kar dete hain.

2. High-Frequency Transitive Verbs (Do NOT Add Prepositions!):
- Discuss: Mamle par charcha karna. [Direct Object: discuss the matter]
  - Incorrect: *We will discuss about the pending writ petitions tomorrow.
  - Correct: We will discuss the pending writ petitions tomorrow.
- Enter (Physical Space): Kamre ya bhavan ke andar jana. [Direct Object: enter the room]
  - Incorrect: *The judicial magistrate entered into the courtroom at 10:30 AM.
  - Correct: The judicial magistrate entered the courtroom at 10:30 AM.
  - Legitimate Exception: 'Enter into' tab valid hota hai jab entry metaphorical, abstract ya legal ho: 'The two IT firms entered into a maintenance agreement.'
- Reach: Kisi sthan par pahunchna. [Direct Object: reach the station]
  - Incorrect: *The inspection team reached to the High Court premises on time.
  - Correct: The inspection team reached the High Court premises on time.
  - Legitimate Exception: 'Reach out to someone' ek alag phrasal verb hai jiska matlab help mangna ya sampark karna hota hai.
- Order (Goods/Food): Saman ya khana mangwana. [Direct Object: order food]
  - Incorrect: *The staff ordered for fresh computer hardware.
  - Correct: The staff ordered fresh computer hardware.
  - Note: Agar 'order' Noun ban jaye toh 'for' lag sakta hai: 'He placed an order for computer hardware.' Lekin Verb ke roop mein koi preposition nahi lagta!
- Resemble: Kisi ke saman dikhna ya shakal milna. [Direct Object: resemble someone]
  - Incorrect: *The young clerk resembles to his father.
  - Correct: The young clerk resembles his father.
- Approach: Kisi ke paas aana ya sampark karna. [Direct Object: approach someone]
  - Incorrect: *The petitioner approached to the High Court for relief.
  - Correct: The petitioner approached the High Court for relief.
- Emphasize: Kisi baat par zor dena. [Direct Object: emphasize a point]
  - Incorrect: *The Chief Justice emphasized on the need for speedy trials.
  - Correct: The Chief Justice emphasized the need for speedy trials.
  - Note: Noun form mein 'emphasis' preposition 'ON' leta hai: 'lay emphasis ON speedy trials'. Lekin Verb form mein strictly zero preposition!
- Demand: Maang karna. [Direct Object: demand an explanation]
  - Incorrect: *The registrar demanded for an explanation from the clerk.
  - Correct: The registrar demanded an explanation from the clerk.
  - Note: Noun form mein 'demand for' valid hota hai ('a heavy demand for IT staff').
- Describe: Varnan karna. [Direct Object: describe the incident]
  - Incorrect: *The witness described about the accident in detail.
  - Correct: The witness described the accident in detail.
- Accompany: Kisi ke sath jana. [Direct Object: accompany someone]
  - Incorrect: *The advocate accompanied with his junior to the chamber.
  - Correct: The advocate accompanied his junior to the chamber.

3. Do Not Overgeneralize:
Aisa nahi hai ki ye verbs English mein kabhi preposition dekh hi nahi sakti. Jaise bataya gaya, 'enter into an agreement' valid hai; 'reach out to people' valid hai; 'order for someone' tab ho sakta hai jab kisi ke behad par order place ho raha ho. Lekin jab verb apne standard core meaning mein direct object le rahi ho, tab preposition lagana fatal pleonastic error hai.

sections.formulaNote: THE DIRECT OBJECT LAW: discuss (NO about), enter room (NO into), order food (NO for), reach place (NO to), resemble (NO to/with), emphasize (NO on). Eliminate these redundant prepositions instantly.

sections.title: Prepositions Followed by Nouns, Pronouns, and -Ing Forms (Gerunds)
sections.summary: Preposition ke baad mandatory Gerund (-ing), 'to' as preposition vs 'to' as infinitive marker, aur exam exceptions.
sections.content:
English grammar ka ek universal rule hai: Kisi bhi Preposition ke turant baad agar koi Verb aati hai, toh wo hamesha GERUND (-ing form) mein honi chahiye, kabhi bhi bare verb (V1) mein nahi ho sakti:
Formula: Preposition + Verb-ing (Gerund)
- 'He is fond of reading legal biographies.' (of + reading)
- 'She insisted on submitting the rejoinder today.' (on + submitting)
- 'The security prevented them from entering the inner hall.' (from + entering)
- 'He is interested in learning automated legal software.' (in + learning)

1. The Tricky 'TO' Distinction: Preposition vs Infinitive Marker:
Candidates ko sabse zyada confusion tab hota hai jab preposition 'TO' hota hai. English mein 'to' do alag functions perform karta hai:
- Function 1: Infinitive Marker (to + V1) ➔ 'He wants to learn.' / 'The court decided to adjourn.' (Yahan 'to' preposition nahi hai, infinitive ka hissa hai).
- Function 2: Preposition ➔ Expressions jahan 'to' preposition ke roop mein fixed hota hai. Jab 'to' preposition hota hai, toh uske baad aane wali verb strictly GERUND (-ing) hogi, V1 bilkul nahi!

2. High-Frequency Fixed Expressions with 'TO' + Gerund (-ing):
In expressions ko examiner frequently test karta hai kyunki candidates 'to' dekhkar aadat ke anusar V1 laga dete hain:
- look forward to + V-ing: 'I look forward to hearing your judgment.' [NOT: *look forward to hear]
- be accustomed to + V-ing: 'He is accustomed to working long hours in the court.' [NOT: *accustomed to work]
- be used to + V-ing: 'She is used to dealing with technical server issues.' [NOT: *used to deal]
- object to + V-ing: 'The advocate objected to introducing new oral evidence.' [NOT: *objected to introduce]
- with a view to + V-ing: 'The registry was upgraded with a view to improving efficiency.' [NOT: *with a view to improve]
- prone to + V-ing: 'This old operating system is prone to crashing during peak hours.' [NOT: *prone to crash]
- addicted to + V-ing: 'He is addicted to gambling.'
- devoted to / dedicated to + V-ing: 'He is dedicated to serving the judiciary.'
- confessed to + V-ing: 'The accused confessed to committing the robbery.'

3. Preposition + Pronoun Case:
Jaise Lesson 11 mein dekha gaya, preposition ke baad aane wala pronoun hamesha OBJECTIVE CASE mein hota hai:
- 'Depend on him' (NOT: *depend on he)
- 'Insisted on my/his submitting' (Gerund ke pehle possessive adjective lagta hai: 'insisted on his coming on time').

categories.name: Prepositional 'TO' + V-ing (The Big Trap)
categories.detail: look forward to meeting, accustomed to living, object to paying, with a view to purchasing, committed to providing, addicted to drinking.

dimensions.name: How to Test if 'TO' is a Preposition
dimensions.description: Ek simple cognitive test jo exam hall mein turant decide kar deta hai.

categories.name: The Noun Substitution Test
categories.detail: Agar 'to' ke baad koi Noun (jaise 'it' ya 'the decision') fit ho sakta hai, toh 'to' preposition hai aur verb aane par -ing lega: 'I look forward to IT' (Valid) ➔ 'look forward to meeting'; 'He is accustomed to IT' (Valid) ➔ 'accustomed to working'.

categories.name: The Infinitive Failure
categories.detail: 'He wants it' (Valid, par 'wants to it' invalid) ➔ 'wants to work' (Infinitive, so V1).

sections.formulaNote: GERUND CONCORD LAW: Preposition + V-ing. Especially after: 'look forward to', 'accustomed to', 'object to', 'with a view to' ➔ ALWAYS use V-ing (never V1!).

sections.title: Fixed Prepositions in Administrative & Legal Contexts
sections.summary: Rajasthan High Court exams ke liye high-yield statutory, judicial aur administrative vocabulary collocations.
sections.content:
Rajasthan High Court System Assistant examination mein judicial aur administrative context ke fixed prepositions ka weightage sabse high hota hai. Court proceedings, notifications, service rules, aur official circulars mein aane wale core collocations:

1. Compliance & Statutory Adherence:
- abide by: Court ke order, rules, ya contract ki sharton par kayam rehna ('All citizens must abide by the constitution and court verdicts.')
- adhere to: Niyam, policy ya timeline par dridh rehna ('The registry must strictly adhere to the roster guidelines.')
- comply with: Guidelines, statutory provisions ya directives ka palan karna ('The IT infrastructure must comply with national cyber security norms.')
- in accordance with: Ke anusaar ('The appointment was made in accordance with the Rajasthan High Court Staff Rules.')
- pursuant to: Ke anusaran mein / ke tahet ('Pursuant to the directions of the Division Bench, an affidavit was submitted.')
- in conformity with: Ke anuroop ('The judgment is in conformity with earlier apex court decisions.')

2. Judicial Offence, Accusation & Verdict:
- acquit of: Kisi jurm ya apradh se ba-izzat bari karna ('The learned sessions judge acquitted the accused of all charges.') [NOT: *acquitted from!]
- convict of: Kisi apradh ka doshi thehrana ('He was convicted of murder and forgery.') [NOT: *convicted for!]
- charge with: Kisi jurm ka arop lagana ('The public prosecutor charged him with criminal conspiracy.') [Note: accused OF, but charged WITH!]
- exonerate from: Kisi dosh ya obligation se mukt karna ('The departmental inquiry exonerated the officer from all allegations.')
- implicate in: Kisi apradh ya shadyantra mein ghasitna ('The co-accused attempted to implicate the registrar in the scam.')

3. Authority, Jurisdiction & Vesting:
- vested in: Kisi pad, authority ya body ke andar shaktiyaan nihit hona ('Judicial power is vested in the courts of law.')
- vested with: Kisi authority ko shaktiyon se susajjit karna ('The Registrar General is vested with wide administrative powers.')
- incumbent on / upon: Kisi padadhikari ke liye anivarya ya farz hona ('It is incumbent on the System Assistant to maintain server backups daily.')
- cognizance of: Kisi apradh ka aadhikarik sangyan lena ('The magistrate took cognizance of the offence under Section 190.')
- jurisdiction over: Kisi kshetra ya mamle par aadhikarik kanooni adhikar ('The Rajasthan High Court has territorial jurisdiction over the entire state.')

4. Disposal, Tampering & Prohibition:
- dispose of: Kisi file, petition ya property ka nistaran karna ('The Division Bench disposed of fifty writ petitions in a single session.') [Note: Strictly single 'f' - dispose OF, NEVER *dispose off!]
- tamper with: Kisi official document, software, ya evidence ke sath chhedchhad karna ('Attempting to tamper with digital court records is a non-bailable offence.')
- refrain from: Kisi aacharan se swayam ko door rakhna ('Advocates must refrain from making unverified public statements.')
- abstain from: Kisi aadat ya voting se door rehna ('Two members chose to abstain from voting on the resolution.')
- connive at: Kisi galat kaam ya corruption ko chupchap ignore karke sahmati dena ('The supervising officer connived at the irregularities.')
- derogation of: Kisi adhikar ya rule ki kami ya upeksha ('The new order is in derogation of fundamental statutory rights.')

dimensions.name: High Court Exam High-Risk Traps
dimensions.description: Specific spelling aur lexical traps jo court exams mein aksar bante hain.

categories.name: Dispose OF vs Dispose OFF
categories.detail: Examiner hamesha 'dispose off' likhta hai jo completely galat hai. Sahi legal spelling strictly 'dispose OF' (single 'f') hai.

categories.name: Acquit OF (Not From)
categories.detail: Hindi mein 'aarop SE bari kiya' bolte hain, isliye log *acquitted from charges chunte hain. English mein strictly 'acquitted OF charges' hota hai.

categories.name: Charged WITH vs Accused OF
categories.detail: Accused hamesha 'OF' leta hai ('accused of bribery'); Charged hamesha 'WITH' leta hai ('charged with bribery').

sections.formulaNote: STATUTORY MASTER KEYS: (1) 'dispose OF' (single 'f' always!); (2) 'abide BY' the rules; (3) 'acquit OF' the crime; (4) 'charged WITH' the offence; (5) 'tamper WITH' records.
